channel.title: AI - Ars Technica
channel.description: Serving the Technologist since 1998. News, reviews, and analysis.

item.title: Nvidia's $100 billion OpenAI deal has seemingly vanished
item.description: Two AI giants shake market confidence after investment fails to materialize.

item.title: X office raided in France's Grok probe; Elon Musk summoned for questioning
item.description: Paris prosecutor: Illegal content probe includes pornographic images of minors.

item.title: Xcode 26.3 adds support for Claude, Codex, and other agentic tools via MCP
item.description: With Model Context Protocol (MCP), this works with more than Codex/Claude, too.

item.title: Senior staff departing OpenAI as firm prioritizes ChatGPT development
item.description: Resources are redirected from long-term research toward improving the flagship chatbot.

item.title: The rise of Moltbook suggests viral AI prompts may be the next big security threat
item.description: We don't need self-replicating AI models to have problems, just self-replicating prompts.

item.title: SpaceX acquires xAI, plans to launch a massive satellite constellation to power it
item.description: "This marks not just the next chapter, but the next book in SpaceX and xAI's mission."

item.title: OpenAI picks up pace against Claude Code with new Codex desktop app
item.description: The macOS app does everything the CLI, IDE, and web interfaces do.

item.title: AI agents now have their own Reddit-style social network, and it's getting weird fast
item.description: Moltbook lets 32,000 AI bots trade jokes, tips, and complaints about humans.

item.title: Developers say AI coding tools work—and that's precisely what worries them
item.description: Ars spoke to several software devs about AI and found enthusiasm tempered by unease.

item.title: Web portal leaves kids' chats with AI toy open to anyone with Gmail account
item.description: Just about anyone with a Gmail account could access Bondu chat transcripts.

item.title: How often do AI chatbots lead users down a harmful path?
item.description: Anthropic's latest paper on "user disempowerment" has some troubling findings.

item.title: Google Project Genie lets you create interactive worlds from a photo or prompt
item.description: Project Genie lets you generate new worlds 60 seconds at a time, but only if you pay for AI Ultra.

item.title: New OpenAI tool renews fears that “AI slop” will overwhelm scientific research
item.description: New "Prism" workspace launches just as studies show AI-assisted papers are flooding journals with diminished quality.

item.title: Does Anthropic believe its AI is conscious, or is that just what it wants Claude to think?
item.description: We have no proof that AI models suffer, but Anthropic acts like they might for training purposes.

item.title: US cyber defense chief accidentally uploaded secret government info to ChatGPT
item.description: Congress recently grilled the acting chief on mass layoffs and a failed polygraph.

item.title: Google begins rolling out Chrome's "Auto Browse" AI agent today
item.description: The Auto Browse agent is available to AI Pro and AI Ultra subscribers, but there are some limits.

item.title: Report: China approves import of high-end Nvidia AI chips after weeks of uncertainty
item.description: Over 400,000 H200 chips coming to tech giants as China tries to balance tech needs with self-reliance.

item.title: Users flock to open source Moltbot for always-on AI, despite major risks
item.description: The open source "Jarvis" chats via WhatsApp but requires access to your files and accounts.

item.title: AI Overviews gets upgraded to Gemini 3 with a dash of AI Mode
item.description: AI Overviews may get it right more often with the move to Gemini 3.

item.title: OpenAI spills technical details about how its AI coding agent works
item.description: Unusually detailed post explains how OpenAI handles the Codex agent loop.
